title: "How common are direct-method cash flow statements?"

author: Ian D. Gow
date: 2026-06-11
date-format: "D MMMM YYYY"

This note illustrates how data compiled using my `dera.pq` R package can be used to analyse XBRL data from SEC filings. Using these data, I show that direct-method cash flow statements have become even rarer for US firms than they were in 2011, when the last *Accounting Trends and Techniques* survey was published.

[Read the note (PDF)](cash-flows.pdf){.btn .btn-primary}

## Source code

The complete [Quarto source](cash-flows.qmd), [bibliography](cash-flows-references.bib), and [citation style](cash-flows.csl) are available to download. Save all three files in the same directory to render the note. Running the analysis requires the R packages used in the source and a local DERA Notes Parquet repository configured through `DATA_DIR`.

This is a copy of the note dated 11 June 2026 from the [cash-flows repository](https://github.com/iangow/cash-flows). The PDF retains the results from that version.
